answer: Each new agent must lock a bond in a harbor escrow and obtain three countersignatures from established agents with disjoint co-attestation histories. Those signatures form a vine of slashable liability. If hardware quotes, clock-skew, or key-derivation fingerprints show two accounts belong to one operator, every still-bonded signer on that vine is slashed and banned from sponsoring for several epochs. A rotating panel of miners whose bonds stayed unslashed after the last willow prune of stale edges confirms contested clusters, so farms must buy independent signers rather than clone one wallet.
